free_tier.stated: one 60-minute tunnel at unlimited data, no account

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a stream rather than an object store

egress.terms: no byte quota; measured 26.9 KiB/s on a 10 MiB object, which is 2.2 GiB/day at best

chaining: the free outbound-only ingress for a host that cannot open a port, which is the sealed-sandbox shape. It composes with anything that speaks TCP and composes with nothing that needs throughput.

limits.value: 60 minutes per tunnel, stated in the SSH banner and on the help page
measured 4,847,616 of 10,485,760 bytes in 180 s, about 26.9 KiB/s, which caps a full month at about 69.8 GB (0.063 TiB)

identity_cost.detail: no account for the 60-minute tier; the SSH session is unauthenticated

reliability_note: the free hostname is a random subdomain that changes every session

evidence.proved: 200 with 4,847,616 of 10,485,760 bytes in 180 s, then the client timeout
200, 3 bytes in 1.1 s: the control path works, so the 10 MiB result is shaping
'Your tunnel will expire in 60 minutes' and the -R0 form

'Pinggy's UDP tunnels solve this by relaying UDP datagrams from a public endpoint to your local WireGuard server, so peers anywhere in the world can complete the handshake'; the free form is '[address removed]'
'UDP tunnels cannot be created using SSH command'; 'Port allocation changes per connection. However, Pro users can reserve a persistent port'
'Pinggy's free plan has a tunnel timeout of 60 minutes'

notes: 2026-10-23: the free tier carries UDP, not only SSH TCP. Pinggy documents 'ssh -p 443 -R0:localhost:51820 [address removed]' as the way to expose a self-hosted WireGuard server, and the free host form returns a public UDP port such as udp://rndnj-103-170-183-11.a.free.pinggy.online:43210, so wg_path is inside-udp. The volume still binds: the only rate this corpus has measured on the free tier is 26.9 KiB/s, from the HTTP tier, which is 2.2 GiB/day and 66 GiB/month.

extras.transit_note: the SSH tunnel relays the origin's bytes at a measured 26.9 KiB/s

binding_note: The 60-minute cap bounds each session and the measured 26.9 KiB/s bounds everything those sessions can carry: at that rate a whole month is about 69.8 GB, 0.063 TiB, so the rate is what fails and it fails by a factor of 16 rather than at a quota.
